summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and chronic Foley catheter use was admitted with left flank pain, cloudy urine, and nausea, diagnosed with acute pyelonephritis due to E. coli, and treated with IV meropenem followed by ceftriaxone and transitioned to oral cefpodoxime. She also presented with constipation causing abdominal pain and distension, which worsened and required NG tube decompression and manual disimpaction, with subsequent improvement on aggressive bowel regimen. Her INR was subtherapeutic for her known right leg DVT, so she was bridged with Lovenox and restarted on warfarin with outpatient monitoring arranged. Metabolic acidosis resolved with IV fluids. She was discharged to a shelter with medication adjustments, including continued warfarin, antibiotics, and enhanced bowel regimen, with close follow-up for INR and primary care.
